mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three consecutive months of >0.5% INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and accelerating inflation, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their 6-month moving averages signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both exceed 6-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and RSAFS exceed their 6-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% for four consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to higher discount rates.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE remains below 4.5% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a robust housing recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports broader economic growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST exceeds 12-month moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during six consecutive months where HOUST exceeds its 12-month moving average.
